The money showed up. The interactivity didn't

Experiential spending is at a record. Most of what it buys is still a photo op.

01 Field notes

Record spend, thin interaction

Global experiential spend passed 128 billion dollars in 2024, its first time above the levels seen before the pandemic, and 51 percent of brands say they will spend more through 2026. But walk the floor and most immersive activations are the same thing dressed up: a branded backdrop, a hashtag, a queue for a photo. That is reach wearing a costume, not participation.

02
In the lab

The activations that convert answer back

The activations that convert are multisensory and responsive. They change based on what the visitor does. A spectacle you only watch is expensive reach. An experience that answers you is a relationship.

03 Craft

Meanwhile, done right

The World Cup 2026 activations that landed were not the biggest screens. They were the ones that gave fans something to do. U.S. World Cup experiences are reportedly up 403 percent versus 2022, with attendance up 572 percent. Demand is not the problem. Passivity is.
